the FhbB protein of the T. dentalis 35405 strain is a more potent ligand for factor H than that of strain 33521 and the FhbB structure of strain 35405 is more amenable to FH binding than strain 33521.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function and regulation of the FhbBs of T. dentalis strains 33521 (dentilisin negative) and 35405 (dentilisin positive).
the identification of bacterial factors that influence the development and severity and of periodontal diseases.
the molecular mechanisms of the interactions between Treponema dencitola and the host, and the impact these interactions have on periodontal disease progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two FhbB proteins are very similar, but not identical, in their ability to interact with FH.
the FhbB of T. dentalis 35405 binds FH with a higher affinity than the FhbB from strain 33521.
the FhbB from T. denticolas strain 33521 has the ability to bind FH with a higher affinity and a higher binding rate constant than the FhbB protein from T. dentalis strain 35405.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sequence of the FhbBs is conserved but that there are differences in their properties that may impact on the interaction of T. dentincola with FH.
the FhbB protein of T. denticola is a highly divergent protein with a unique ligand binding site that has evolved to facilitate binding and cleavage of FH.
FhbB of T. dentincola is a conserved protein, but that the sequence differences between strains 33521 (dentilisin negative) and 35405 (dentilisin positive) have significant impact on its function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FH binding site on FhbB is conserved and that the FhbB-FH interaction is a key determinant for the survival of T. dentincola in the oral environment.
the FhbB protein is highly conserved in the strains of T. dentricola examined.
sequence divergence in the FhbB protein can have significant consequences for the interaction with FH.
